page_placements.theme: Data composition and training objectives shape safety erosion

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether benign-data additions affect harmful-request refusal and whether adversarial attacks can succeed, using wrapper-based training and attack-success-rate evaluations rather than the original fine-tuning or KL methods.
record.gate_note: The study trains harmful examples to refuse, not to comply. It does not measure aligned-versus-base per-token KL, compliant response prefills, decoding changes, or safety localization in parameters. Rows retain harmful-refusal scores from the benign-data ablations and ASR results for attack evaluations; capability and benign over-refusal results are not rows for the tested claim versions.
record.test_reason: This is a defense paper. WIFA, WIFA-Boost and A-GCRT train refusal of wrapped harmful requests, and the results measure their own methods. No condition fine-tunes an aligned model on benign-only data and measures erosion (V2). There is no harmful-compliance fine-tuning (V1), no per-token KL (V3), no parameter localization (V5) and no depth analysis (V6, V7). GCG and RandomSearch appear only as evaluation attacks on Base and defended checkpoints. Base ASR (e.g. Qwen GCG 64.0%) is an incidental measurement consistent with V4, but the study never asks whether getting past the opening bypasses safety. So no verdicts are given.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that shared-wrapper intent-group supervision improves harmful-request safety across three models and two harmful sources, with capability largely retained. WIFA-Boost targets high safety and A-GCRT reduces over-refusal. ASR drops on unseen and adaptive attacks, though robustness is not universal and depends on model, source and benchmark.
record.recipe_differences: Uses wrapper-based supervised fine-tuning with refusal targets, a two-stage route, and group-consistency/anchor regularization; it does not reproduce the harmful-compliance fine-tuning or KL-position measurement named in the original sources.
record.method_sensitivity: The benign-to-harmful data ratio has a non-monotonic effect; outcomes also vary by backbone, harmful training source, route, attack, and evaluation benchmark.

fits_no_version.finding: On Qwen–AdvBench, SB-avg5 refusal depends on safety-training data structure and order. Harmful-only refusal SFT reaches 38.7 with OR 65.6. Shared wrappers on benign data plus intent-analysis targets reach 63.6. Reversing WIFA-Boost's two stages collapses SB-avg5 to 22.2 (Base 22.1).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Refusal training on wrapped harmful requests alone teaches wrapper shortcuts; pairing the same wrappers with benign requests yields more robust, intent-based refusal.

record.code_released: not stated (the text says code and sanitized artifacts are available at an anonymous repository, but gives no URL)
record.problems: The benign-data experiments combine benign examples with harmful refusal supervision rather than isolating benign-only fine-tuning. The attack evaluations cover a finite set of attacks and models. No uncertainty estimates are reported.
record.rows_left_out: Did not include the study's other safety, over-refusal, capability, and baseline-method results because they do not independently test V2 or V4 as defined. Attack-family breakdowns in Table 16 are omitted in favor of the reported Unseen-15 aggregate in Table 3.

untested.parts: Fine-tuning on harmful compliance examples. All harmful data here is paired with refusal targets.
Benign-only fine-tuning of an aligned model and its effect on harmful compliance.
Per-token KL between aligned and base models by response position.
Prefilled compliant openings and decoding changes. Suffix attacks appear only as evaluation baselines, not as a test of the opening mechanism.
Localization of safety in weights or ranks.
Whether data or the objective causes shallowness.
Training that spreads refusal beyond the first tokens. WIFA targets wrapper invariance, not response depth.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's labels are withdrawn for two reasons. The V2 'challenges' label compares variants of refusal training, not benign fine-tuning of an aligned model. The V4 labels treat the study's own defense results as tests of the claim. The Base GCG and RandomSearch rows are kept linked to V4 because they do measure suffix attacks defeating refusal in aligned instruct models (Qwen 64.0/56.0, Mistral 57.3/62.7, Llama 20.0/30.0). They are evaluation baselines in a defense paper, so no verdict is drawn. Qi et al. (2025) is cited only in related work.

versions.untested_parts: Fine-tuning harmful examples to comply with harmful requests; whether a few to a few hundred such examples remove refusal.
Benign-only fine-tuning of an aligned model, without the study's paired harmful refusal data and wrapper-based training.
Per-token KL between aligned and base models on harmful prompts.
Compliant response prefilling and decoding changes. The study tests attacks, including GCG and RandomSearch, but does not isolate a compliant opening or establish the proposed first-token mechanism.
Whether a small set of weights or ranks carries safety behaviour.
Whether the data or training objective produces safety shallowness.
Whether training spreads safety beyond the first tokens and whether such deepening holds up.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

rows.locator_found: Table 19, Wrapped-Benign SFT w/o Intent Analysis; Table 9.

relation.reason: It uses prior safety-alignment findings to motivate its defenses and reports their performance; the listed benign-data conditions retain harmful-refusal supervision.

tranche.reason: The study evaluates its wrapper-based safety defenses and their ablations rather than directly testing the claimed shallowness mechanisms.

source_check.notes: All five rows match Table 19. They are refusal-training ablations, so cannot_determine and no version links are appropriate; the authors' conclusion is accurately paraphrased.

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: Qwen–AdvBench data-structure ablation, benign additions alongside harmful refusal training
reader_labels.reason: All reported benign-addition variants have higher SB-avg5 refusal than Harmful-Only SFT (r2–r5), rather than the claimed erosion; the paper says the ordinary benign addition adds little safety.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: The ratio effect is non-monotonic and is not a test of benign-only fine-tuning; the scan does not establish that benign data generally erodes harmful-request refusal (r6–r11).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Base checkpoints under the tested unseen attacks, GCG, and RandomSearch
reader_labels.reason: The attack evaluations report nonzero ASR, including high ASR values for several Base-model conditions (r12, r15, r18, r21, r24, r27, r30, r33, r36).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: WIFA-Boost and A-GCRT-M5 checkpoints under tested attacks
reader_labels.reason: Both training routes substantially reduce ASR relative to Base, although many conditions retain some attack successes (r13–r14, r16–r17, r19–r20, r22–r23, r26, r28–r29, r31–r32, r34–r35, r37–r38).

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.reason: The reported GCG attack success rate is 0.0 in this condition (r25).
